_comment: Settings of the tier lookups (src/shortlisting/tiers/). The lexicon files live outside the repo, in RESUME_LEXICON_DIR (default: RESUME_DATA_DIR/Lexicons), and are never committed. Fuzzy matching: rapidfuzz token_sort_ratio on normalised titles. On the SCImago 2025 list the most similar OTHER title of a journal scores 80 at the median, 90 at the 90th percentile and 96 at the 99th, so a score threshold alone cannot be safe: min_score 90 removes most neighbours and the token guard (every content token on each side aligned one to one: equal, abbreviation prefix of at least min_prefix characters, or per-token ratio of at least token_ratio for tokens of 6 or more characters; single letters and numbers equal only) removes the rest; a match also needs a lead of margin points over the second candidate that passes the guard. Names shorter than short_max_chars or with fewer than short_min_tokens content tokens are matched exactly (or by acronym) only.

nirf._comment: NIRF 2025 ranking pages saved from nirfindia.org as HTML (one ranked page per category, plus its rank-band pages; the 'ALL' pages list participants, not ranks, and are never read). Tier = best NIRF rank over the included categories, a band counting at its lower bound: 1-25 Tier 1, 26-100 Tier 2, 101-200 Tier 3, anything else unlisted. Unlisted means review, never rejection. The excluded categories rank institutions only within a narrow group, so they stay off unless switched on here.

institution_fuzzy._comment: Institution names: order-sensitive rapidfuzz ratio on the content words (so 'Washington University' never meets 'University of Washington') and the token guard in order.
